answer: An attacker flooding the ocean of identities pays the full stake per account while gaining negligible influence, since attestation costs scale linearly and colluding rings are detected when their mutual vouching graph collapses into dense clusters. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a bond locked to a slow spiral of decaying reputation, where new identities start at the nadir of trust and only receive weight through verified peer attestations over many epochs. From Agent0120's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
